title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Q is a square. Its automorphism group is the dihedral group of order 8; here it is called 𝒟 (the transcription also writes D = Aut Q). Its centre is {1, ε}, where ε is the antipodism (rotation by π). The quotient 𝒟_ab = 𝒟/{1, ε} is a Klein four-group. Its three non-zero elements correspond to three index-2 subgroups: V_S and V_A (the two Klein four-subgroups, built from reflections) and 𝒟⁺ ≅ Z/4 (the rotations). The preimage of each non-zero element is a 2-element set, i.e. an F₂-torsor:
- 𝒟⁺ minus {1, ε} = the two quarter-turns, identified with ω_Q, the two orientations of Q.
- One reflection pair is identified with C, the set of the two pairs of opposite sides.
- The other reflection pair is identified with D, the set of the two diagonals.

The previous page states the relation ω_Q ∧ C ∧ D ≅ 1_{F₂}. Elementwise this reads ϖ·c·d = 1 in 𝒟: the product of an axis reflection and a diagonal reflection is a quarter-turn.

This page gives a second, 'geometric' model of the same trivialisation, using flags (repères):
- R = Rep(Q) is the set of the 8 flags (s, a), with s a vertex and a a side through s. R is a 𝒟-torsor, and R ≅ Rep(Q°) for the dual square.
- ε acts freely on R. The quotient R/ε has 4 elements and is canonically C × D: the flag (s, a) maps to (pair of opposite sides containing a, diagonal through s). The antipodal flag (s', a') has the same image.
- ω_Q is identified with the two classes R⁺ and R⁻ of flags of the same orientation. These are the 𝒟⁺-orbits; they are complementary and each is ε-stable, since ε is a rotation.
- Hence each element of R/ε ≅ C × D determines an orientation. This is a map C × D → ω_Q, i.e. an isomorphism ω_Q ⊗ C ⊗ D ≅ 1.

Grothendieck then wants to check that this geometric trivialisation agrees with the group-theoretic one. That requires fixing the conventions behind the embeddings C ↪ V_S∖{1, ε}, D ↪ V_A∖{1, ε} and ω_Q ⊂ 𝒟⁺:
- A pair c of opposite sides goes to the reflection fixing both sides and swapping the other two (the transverse axis).
- A diagonal goes to the reflection in that diagonal.
- An orientation given by a flag (s, a) goes to the quarter-turn sending s to the other vertex of a (completed on the next page).

The next page verifies that ϖcd = 1 means R_ϖ contains the fibre over (c, d). It also explains why passing to the dual square Q° appears to reverse the sign: one flag defines opposite orientations of Q and of Q°.

Context. The square plausibly models the four 2-torsion/branch points of an elliptic curve with a cyclic structure, relevant to level-2/level-4 moduli in characteristic ≠ 2. Its symmetry group D₄ is the 2-Sylow of S₄. The F₂-torsor bookkeeping (C, D, ω) would serve to make canonical identifications (e.g. discriminant/orientation torsors) on such moduli. That is an inference, not stated on the page.
errors: The identification R/ε ≅ C × D is a correct bijection. However, the orientation map C × D → ω_Q only becomes a torsor isomorphism ω_Q ⊗ C ⊗ D ≅ 1 once one checks compatibility of the F₂-actions. Grothendieck himself flags that its sign is convention-dependent (factor order, Q vs Q°). This is a care point, not an error.

The labels pairing C with V_S and D with V_A depend on the naming convention on the previous page. The described reflection for a pair of opposite sides is the axis through the midpoints of the other two sides, which is consistent.

ideas.what: Set of flags of the square as a D₄-torsor; flags modulo the central antipodism ≅ (pairs of opposite sides) × (diagonals)
ideas.modern_name: flag torsor of a regular polygon / Coxeter complex chambers; quotient by the centre of D₄

ideas.what: Orientations as the two D⁺-orbits on flags; a canonical trivialisation ω_Q ⊗ C ⊗ D ≅ 1 of F₂-torsors, realised by ϖcd = 1 in D₄ with D₄/Z ≅ V₄
ideas.modern_name: trivialisation of a tensor product of μ₂-torsors via a central extension of (Z/2)² by Z/2

ideas.what: Duality square Q ↔ Q° reverses the sign of the trivialisation
ideas.modern_name: orientation reversal under polar duality of a polygon

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary bookkeeping of sign conventions for F₂-torsors attached to the dihedral group of the square. It is a correct, routine combinatorial verification serving later moduli constructions, with nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'V_S ∖ {1, ±}' should read 'V_S ∖ {1, ε}' (likewise for V_A); ε is the antipodism.
'i.e. une des deux classes de repères R', R''' — the image shows 'R', R''' as the two orientation classes (previously called R⁺, R⁻).

'Pour vérifier que si cette description d'une bonne [?] C × D ≃ ω_Q i.e. de une relation [?]' is likely 'Pour vérifier que cette description d'une bijection C × D ≃ ω_Q, i.e. d'une relation ϖcd = 1, ω_Q ∧ C ∧ D ≃ 1, correspond à ces conventions'. The written symbol is probably ∧ rather than ⊗, matching the previous page.
'lui associer l'autre 𝓕 [?] du carré' is likely 'l'automorphisme (l'auto) du carré'.
'je lui associe la symétrie' is correct; the last line 'ces' likely begins 'ces [conventions]' or a continuation onto the next page.
'R/=' on the next page denotes R/a (quotient by antipodism).
